purpose: Graph cases for a single-arm protocol with an informational welcome component and a daily check-in. Each case applies its deliveries in order to a receiver that starts empty and holds definitions.json. Every delivery passes the official FHIR Validator; the expected outcome of each delivery is either the outcome of every occurrence it carries or the graph rules that reject it. Scripts/validate-study-graph.py applies the cases and Tests/test_study_graph.py checks them.

cases.purpose: An occurrence is assigned, then completed by one accepted response with an exact version-specific result link.
Retransmitting the accepted completion unchanged is accepted again without a second completion.
A known occurrence identifier sent with another performance window is a conflicting reuse.
Two occurrences of one component revision with one window remain two occurrences.
Occurrences of a later enrollment have new identifiers; reusing an identifier of the earlier enrollment is a conflict.
A correction links a new version of the same response; the occurrence keeps its identity and is completed once.
A completed occurrence is not completed again by a response with another submission identifier.
A completed occurrence never returns to ready.
An occurrence cancelled with the excused reason before its window opened is accepted.
An occurrence of an informational component, which defines no result, is completed without an output.
An occurrence of a component without a result is not completed after its performance window ended.
A Task that conforms to the base Task profile does not complete a questionnaire occurrence without a result link.
A structurally valid response about another participant does not complete the occurrence.
A structurally valid response to another version of the instrument does not complete the occurrence.
A Task naming a component revision that was never published resolves to no definition and to no protocol action.
A completed Task that links an in-progress response presents a pending completion as accepted.
A result link naming a response version the delivery does not carry resolves to nothing.
A response authored after the performance window ended does not complete the occurrence.
